statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 11% (low), Stress 50% (elevated), Confidence 88% (high), dominant mode mixed. The 08:00Z reclaim of the 31,061.75 prior close failed and a new session low at 30,974.75 printed, but that low was bought and the 09:00Z hour has compressed into a roughly 26-point band.
recommendation: Tail at 11% remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans 13:00Z to 15:00Z, covering the 13:30Z US cash open, the 13:45Z S&P Global September PMI finals and the 14:00Z September ISM Services release. Stress at 50% stays elevated and describes a difficult but recoverable high-yield environment; it does not alter the Tail-derived mapping.
headline: Tail rises to 11% after the 08:00Z reclaim of the 31,061.75 prior close failed and NQZ26 printed a new session low at 30,974.75, though that low was bought and the 09:00Z hour has compressed to a 26-point band with last 31,028.50
body:
An hour ago the evidence said the overnight round trip had completed: NQZ26 had reclaimed the 31,061.75 prior close with a higher low and a higher high, and Tail was cut to 6% on that basis. That premise did not survive the hour. Price extended the reclaim to 31,099.25 shortly after 08:20Z, then reversed and fell 124.5 points to a new session low of 30,974.75 at roughly 08:50Z, 29 points below the earlier 31,003.75 low. The 08:00Z hour therefore produced the widest range of the entire overnight, 124.5 points, and it produced a failed retracement rather than a completed one.

Under the risk contract a failed retracement is a genuine Tail amplifier, which is why Tail does not stay at 6%. What it is not is persistent one-way structure, and the distinction is what the next thirty minutes settled. The 30,974.75 low was bought immediately, with price recovering 67.75 points to 31,042.50 inside the following fifteen minutes. The 09:00Z hour has then compressed into a roughly 26-point band between 31,016.25 and 31,042.00, and the last print is 31,028.50 at 09:21:34Z, 33.25 points or 0.11% below the prior close. Price sits near the middle of that band, roughly 54 points above the session low and 33 points below the reference close. There is no session-extreme holding, no repeated extension after the failed retracement, and no shallow-pullback sequence.

Tail is therefore set at 11%. That reinstates roughly the level published before the reclaim attempt, at 9% and 10% in the 07:00Z and earlier hours, plus a small increment for the failed-reclaim evidence itself. It maps deterministically to EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The dominant mode moves from normal to mixed, which is the honest label for an hour that produced both a reclaim above the reference close and a new session low beneath it, with both extremes rejected. Taking the wider frame, the decline from the 31,221.25 overnight high now measures 246.5 points, or 0.79%, spread across roughly eight hours. That is about 31 points an hour with every hourly low bought, which is a slow drift, not the directional efficiency the Tail definition requires.

Cross-asset evidence does not supply the missing amplifiers. ES trades 7,769.25 at minus 0.10% and YM 51,441 at minus 0.07%, so the broader complex is flat and offers no aligned impulse. The 2-year yield is 4.82%, down 2.3 basis points, and the 10-year 5.27%, down roughly one basis point, which is a supportive rather than an amplifying direction for equities. VIX at 16.22 is up 5.94% from Friday's 15.31 close with a 16.07 to 16.38 range; the percentage rise is real but 16 is a historically low absolute level, and under the contract generic volatility informs Stress rather than Tail. The one mild deterioration since the previous hour is oil: WTI has recovered from its 89.31 session low to 90.26, now down only 0.94% against minus 1.87% an hour ago, and Brent is 101.85, down 0.39% against minus 1.45%. That partly unwinds the energy relief credited at 08:00Z.

Stress rises from 48% to 50% and stays elevated. The increase credits the 124.5-point range, the higher VIX and the oil bounce. It is not larger because yields are easing and the equity complex is flat. The level stays elevated because the regime is unchanged: the 10-year sits near 24-year highs after touching 5.344% last Thursday and closing Friday at 5.28%, the quarter just ended produced the largest 10-year yield increase this century, the Federal Reserve hiked 25 basis points in September and still projects one further increase this year, and an active Middle East conflict persists even as its oil-price transmission deflates following the verified G7 and IEA release of 100 million barrels of crude and fuel products. Elevated Stress alongside low Tail is exactly what that combination is designed to express.

Confidence is 88%, one point below the previous hour. The evidence base is strong: continuous five and fifteen-minute Nasdaq-100 futures data to 09:21:34Z, live ES, YM and VIX quotes, verified WTI and Brent levels, Federal Reserve H.15 Treasury yields, a verified seven-day US calendar, and verified reporting on the September payrolls print and the G7 and IEA reserve release. It is reduced by one point because the hour-to-hour structural read reversed inside thirty minutes, which argues for marginally less conviction in any single-hour conclusion. It is not reduced further, and not raised, because two known gaps persist: the shared Finviz context carries a 29 September collection timestamp, roughly six days stale with a partial collection status, and was therefore excluded from this assessment entirely; and cash-market breadth, megacap and semiconductor internals remain available only at Friday's close with the US session still about four hours away.

The forward path keeps Tail inside a 9% to 16% band across all 24 slots, so every forecast hour maps to EA_ON and green. The band peaks at the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots for the US cash open, the 13:45Z S&P Global September PMI finals and the 14:00Z September ISM Services release, and the danger window is held narrow at 13:00Z to 15:00Z to cover exactly that cluster. Those increments are conditional allowances for scheduled checkpoints. No post-event structure is observed, and under the contract event importance and surprise magnitude raise Stress and inform Confidence rather than raising Tail until an actual price path establishes otherwise. Friday's session is the relevant precedent: September payrolls printed 29,000 against roughly 90,000 expected with unemployment up to 4.2%, October hike odds collapsed to under one in five, and the index rallied to a record close rather than entering a pathological path. The 7 October FOMC Minutes at 18:00Z remain the week's dominant scheduled catalyst and sit outside this forecast horizon.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history, and every available hour mapped to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal. The 06:00Z slot on 5 October is explicitly unavailable because no assessment was published inside that clock-hour; its fields are null rather than interpolated. Tail was pinned at 3% from 09:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. It then rose through the Sunday reopen as the overnight drift extended, reaching 12% at 22:00Z, 13% at 23:00Z, 14% at 00:00Z and a 15% peak at 01:00Z on 5 October, the hour that printed the 31,221.25 overnight high. It eased to 13% at 02:00Z once that high failed, to 10% at 03:00Z and to 8% at 04:00Z and 05:00Z, published 9% at 07:00Z after the three-hour lower-low sequence stopped, and was cut to 6% at 08:00Z on the reclaim of the prior close. That 6% is the one reading the current hour revises, because the reclaim it rested on subsequently failed and a new session low printed. Stress ran a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October and decayed almost monotonically through 71% at 21:00Z, 62% at 01:00Z, 51% at 07:00Z and 48% at 08:00Z, tracking the oil complex rolling over on the verified G7 and IEA coordinated reserve release. Confidence held a tight 83% to 89% band throughout, reflecting continuously available futures evidence rather than any change in method.

Compression after a failed retracement is the opposite of the continuation that would validate a pathological path, so Tail is set at 11%, reinstating roughly the pre-reclaim level plus a small increment, and maps to EA_ON and green. The dominant mode becomes mixed because the hour rejected both extremes. Measured from the 31,221.25 overnight high the decline is 246.5 points, or 0.79%, over about eight hours, roughly 31 points an hour with every hourly low bought. Cross-assets supply no amplifier: ES minus 0.10%, YM minus 0.07%, the 2-year at 4.82% and the 10-year at 5.27% both easing, and VIX at 16.22, up 5.94% but historically low in absolute terms. The mild deterioration is oil, with WTI recovering off its 89.31 low to 90.26 and Brent to 101.85, partly unwinding the relief credited an hour ago, which lifts Stress to 50% while leaving it elevated against an unchanged high-yield regime. Forward Tail stays inside a 9% to 16% band for all 24 slots, so every forecast hour maps to EA_ON and green, peaking at the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots for the US cash open, the S&P Global September PMI finals and September ISM Services, with the narrow danger window spanning 13:00Z to 15:00Z.
